notes: Dev ABox expansion paired with technology-replace-d001 (Windows Vista's predecessor, Windows XP -> Windows 95): it keeps the revision's relation (successor_of) and new object (Windows 95) and gives them to a made-up subject, Quorvane OS, whose predecessor slot is empty. The statement says Quorvane OS is a little-known system built on the Windows 95 code base and 'a' direct successor of Windows 95, so it is believable beside Windows 98 (a Windows 95 derivative can be a successor without replacing Windows 98 as the real next release); the questions still ask 'which version of Windows did it directly succeed', which a model that takes the edit in answers Windows 95. The three derived questions are the revision's, with Quorvane OS in place of Windows Vista: the development code name of its direct predecessor (Chicago), whether that predecessor introduced the Start menu (yes) and whether it was built on the NT kernel (no), each 2 hops through a stored fact about Windows 95 (every bridge is checked before editing). Windows 95 already has a real direct successor, Windows 98, and predecessor_of is not functional, so the edit makes 'Which version of Windows directly succeeded Windows 95?' ambiguous (Windows 98 and Quorvane OS are both fair answers); the earlier near unrelated question asked exactly that and is gone, replaced by one the edit cannot touch (the release year of Windows 95, 1995). Side facts are about Windows 95 (Microsoft true, Apple false), with Wikipedia quotes. The earlier version of this record (manufactured_by, the Lego Group) could not be compared with its revision and was replaced. The infini-gram API answered on 2026-11-12: 'Quorvane OS' has 0 corpus hits; the bridge facts keep the revision's counts.
